game.title: Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen
game.notes: Originally released for Game Boy Advance in 2004; this list targets the digital Nintendo Switch / Switch 2 re-release dated February 27, 2026 (two separate $19.99 SKUs, Pokémon Day/30th anniversary). Genesis Mode: Nintendo platforms have no native achievement/trophy system, and FireRed/LeafGreen have never released on a platform that has one. All Switch-specific mechanical claims in the research dossier rest on secondary gaming press rather than an official Nintendo patch-notes document; treated as medium confidence throughout. Scope decisions, including corrections made after the first audit pass: (1) FRLG-024 (Kanto Pokédex completion) targets the real, in-game-defined 150 species (Mew excluded) rather than an invented lower number. Several of those 150 are version-exclusive wild encounters (e.g. the Vulpix/Growlithe and Oddish/Bellsprout-family splits) and can only be obtained by trading with a second physical Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 running the opposite version over local wireless — this has been inherent to FireRed/LeafGreen's design since the original 2004 cartridges, independent of this platform, and the dependency is disclosed directly on that trophy rather than hidden. (2) A 'catch a Shiny Pokémon' trophy was deliberately NOT included: this generation's flat 1/8192 odds have no Shiny Charm, Masuda Method, or chaining mechanic to offset them, so the chance of one occurring in a normal playthrough is not reasonable under Rule 21. (3) All other multiplayer-dependent content is excluded per Rule 13: the two non-chosen starters and the four trade-evolutions (Kadabra→Alakazam, Machoke→Machamp, Graveler→Golem, Haunter→Gengar) require a second physical Switch and a second copy of the game over local-wireless-only play (no online trading exists on this release, even on Switch 2); the Dodrio Berry Picking minigame is similarly multiplayer-only. None of these are referenced by any trophy. (4) FRLG-016 (Trainer Tower) is framed around beating each mode's default record time within the time limit — the facility's actual completion condition — rather than merely winning a single battle there; it avoids naming which of the four reward items maps to which mode, since that specific mapping is only single-sourced in research. (5) FRLG-019 (Keeper of the Tickets) exists specifically to spotlight the one genuine platform-specific addition found in research: the Mystic and Aurora Tickets are now auto-granted after the player's first Hall of Fame entry, making Ho-Oh, Lugia, and Deoxys reachable through normal play for the first time (previously real-world-event-distribution-only on the original GBA cartridges). (6) FRLG-023 (Mewtwo) deliberately avoids citing an exact Ruby/Sapphire gem requirement for unlocking Cerulean Cave, since research could not resolve whether one or both gems are required — its verification instead references the broader Sevii Islands Network Machine questline. (7) The Rocket Warehouse antagonist's name ('Gideon' in a single low-quality source) could not be confirmed against a primary source and is not used in FRLG-015's text. (8) The Cinnabar Island Mansion's Team Rocket presence could not be confirmed as an active combat beat distinct from its burned-notes lore content, so no trophy is built around it. (9) The Bug-Catching Contest (a Johto-only feature), Voltorb Flip (a Gen IV remake feature), and Pokémon HOME connectivity were all confirmed absent from this game/release and are not referenced anywhere in the list.

trophies.name: A Journey from Pallet Town
trophies.description: Choose your starter Pokémon and set off from Pallet Town.
trophies.verification: The opening story sequence concludes with the chosen starter added to the party.

trophies.name: First Badge
trophies.description: Defeat your first Gym Leader and earn a Badge.
trophies.verification: The Gym Leader's defeat cutscene plays and the Badge is added to the Badge Case.

trophies.name: Echoes from the Past
trophies.description: Revive the Fossil obtained at Mt. Moon — Omanyte or Kabuto — at the Cinnabar Island lab.
trophies.verification: The revived Fossil Pokémon is added to the party after the lab's revival cutscene.

trophies.name: Ghost in the Scope
trophies.description: Clear the Rocket Hideout beneath the Celadon Game Corner and obtain the Silph Scope.
trophies.verification: Defeating Giovanni in the hideout adds the Silph Scope to the Key Items pocket.

trophies.name: Silence No More
trophies.description: Free Mr. Fuji from Team Rocket atop Pokémon Tower and receive the Poké Flute.
trophies.verification: The Poké Flute appears in the Key Items pocket once Mr. Fuji's rescue dialogue concludes.

trophies.name: Coin Collector
trophies.description: Win Coins at the Celadon Game Corner slot machines for the first time.
trophies.verification: The Coin Case balance increases after a winning spin.

trophies.name: Pedal to the Metal
trophies.description: Receive the Bike Voucher from the Vermilion City Pokémon Fan Club Chairman.
trophies.verification: The Bike Voucher appears in the Key Items pocket once the Chairman's dialogue concludes.

trophies.name: A Lesson Well Learned
trophies.description: Learn a move from a Move Tutor for the first time.
trophies.verification: The taught move appears in the Pokémon's move list immediately after the tutor's dialogue.

trophies.name: Beyond the Mainland
trophies.description: Reach the Sevii Islands for the first time aboard the Seagallop Ferry.
trophies.verification: The Town Map updates to show One Island after disembarking.

trophies.name: Safari Catch
trophies.description: Catch a Pokémon inside the Fuchsia City Safari Zone.
trophies.verification: The catch is registered in the Pokédex while still inside the Safari Zone.

trophies.name: A Growing Collection
trophies.description: Register 30 different species as caught in the Pokédex.
trophies.verification: The Pokédex's Owned count reaches 30.

trophies.name: Berries of Three Island
trophies.description: Find a wild Berry hidden in Berry Forest on Three Island.
trophies.verification: The Berry is added to the Bag after being picked up in the forest.

trophies.name: Full Badge Case
trophies.description: Earn all 8 Gym Badges.
trophies.verification: The Badge Case screen shows all 8 Badges present.

trophies.name: Heist at Silph Co.
trophies.description: Defeat Giovanni atop Silph Co. and recover the Master Ball from Team Rocket.
trophies.verification: Giovanni's defeat ends the Silph Co. takeover and the Master Ball is added to the Bag.

trophies.name: Team Rocket, Grounded
trophies.description: Defeat Team Rocket's agents at the Five Island Warehouse and recover the Sapphire.
trophies.verification: Clearing the Rocket Warehouse adds the Sapphire to the Key Items pocket.

trophies.name: Undefeated at the Tower
trophies.description: Clear all four Trainer Tower modes — Single, Double, Mixed, and Knockout — by defeating every trainer in each within that mode's default record time.
trophies.verification: Beating a mode's record time adds that mode's unique one-time reward item to the Bag; all four reward items present confirms every mode cleared.

trophies.name: A Daughter Returned
trophies.description: Rescue Lostelle from Berry Forest and reunite her with her father on Two Island.
trophies.verification: Delivering Lostelle to her father triggers the reunion dialogue and his reward.

trophies.name: Trading Post
trophies.description: Complete an in-game NPC Pokémon trade for the first time.
trophies.verification: The traded-for Pokémon appears in the party immediately after the trade animation.

trophies.name: Keeper of the Tickets
trophies.description: Catch Ho-Oh or Lugia at Navel Rock, or Deoxys at Birth Island, using the Mystic Ticket or Aurora Ticket automatically granted after your first Hall of Fame entry.
trophies.verification: The caught Legendary is registered in the Pokédex.

trophies.name: Halfway There
trophies.description: Register 100 different species as caught in the Pokédex.
trophies.verification: The Pokédex's Owned count reaches 100.

trophies.name: Champion of Kanto
trophies.description: Defeat the Champion at the Pokémon League and enter the Hall of Fame.
trophies.verification: The Champion's defeat triggers Hall of Fame registration.

trophies.name: Three for the Flock
trophies.description: Catch Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres, Kanto's three Legendary birds.
trophies.verification: All three are registered as caught in the Pokédex.

trophies.name: Ghost of Cerulean Cave
trophies.description: Catch Mewtwo deep within Cerulean Cave, after unlocking it through the Sevii Islands' Network Machine questline.
trophies.verification: Mewtwo is added to the party or box and registered in the Pokédex.

trophies.name: Master of Kanto's Dex
trophies.description: Complete the Kanto Pokédex by catching all 150 obtainable species (Mew excluded).
trophies.verification: The Kanto Pokédex Diploma becomes viewable at the Celadon City Mansion, and Professor Oak's rating dialogue confirms 150 species owned.
trophies.notes: Several of the 150 Kanto species are exclusive to the opposite version (e.g. the Vulpix/Growlithe and Oddish/Bellsprout-family splits) and can only be obtained by trading with a second physical Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 running that version over local wireless — inherent to FireRed/LeafGreen's design since the original 2004 release, not something this rerelease changed. Also depends on the one-time catches covered by FRLG-022 (the three Legendary birds) and the two single-encounter wild Snorlax on Routes 12 and 16, hence the missable flag.

trophies.name: Kanto's Living Legend
trophies.description: Earn every other trophy.
trophies.verification: All other trophies earned.
